package.name: Regex
package.description: Regular expressions matched in linear time, with Unicode classes, captures, splitting and replacement

modules.name: Compile
modules.header:
Turning the parsed tree into instructions, by Thompson's construction.
Alternatives become `Split`s whose first branch is the earlier alternative, and repetitions become `Split`s whose
first branch repeats when the repetition is greedy and moves on when it is lazy, so the order of a thread's
branches is the order of preference that leftmost-first matching follows. Counted repetitions are written out in
full, which is what limits the size of a compiled pattern.

modules.name: Dfa
modules.header:
A lazy DFA: each set of threads the matcher can be in becomes one state the first time a search meets it, and the
state each character leads to is remembered, so once a text's states are built a search reads a character with
one table lookup instead of moving every thread. Nothing records where groups matched, so the DFA finds only where
a match ends: forwards for the end of the leftmost-first match, then backwards over the reversed pattern for its
start. The Pike matcher then runs over just that match, and only when its groups are wanted.
A state is the ordered list of instructions its threads continue from, before any of their moves are followed,
with what the moves' assertions need to know about the character before. The next character settles the
assertions about what follows, which is why a transition is computed from a state and a character together.

modules.name: Error
modules.header: Why a pattern could not be compiled, or a search could not run.

modules.name: Machine
modules.header:
Running a compiled pattern over text with Pike's matcher.
Every thread of the match moves forward one character at a time, all together, so the text is read once and the
work per character is bounded by the size of the program: a search takes time proportional to the text times the
pattern, whatever either holds. Threads are kept in order of preference; when one matches, the threads after it
are dropped and those before it run on in case they match too, which gives leftmost-first matching, the answer a
backtracking matcher would give. Each list is a sparse set, so a thread already on it is never added twice and an
empty loop cannot go round forever.

modules.name: Parse
modules.header:
Reading a pattern into a tree of nodes for the compiler.
The grammar is RE2's, less what cannot be matched in linear time. Alternation binds loosest, then concatenation,
then repetition. A node's children are linked through `next`, so a long concatenation or alternation costs no
recursion; only groups and repetitions nest, and their depth is limited.

modules.name: Program
modules.header:
A compiled pattern: the instructions the matcher runs, and the character classes they test.
The instructions are those of Thompson's construction as Pike's matcher runs them. Each one either tests the
character at the current position (`Char`, `CharFold`, `Class`, `Any`, `AnyNotNewline`), or moves without
consuming anything: to another instruction (`Jump`), to two at once with the first preferred (`Split`), by recording
the position in a capture slot (`Save`), or by checking where in the text it is (`Assert`). `Match` ends a match.

modules.name: Regex
modules.header:
Compiled patterns and what can be asked of them: whether text matches, where, with which groups, every match in
turn, the text between matches, and the text with its matches replaced.
A search allocates the storage it works in from the regex's allocator, so a compiled pattern never changes and can
be searched from many threads at once. An iterator keeps its storage for every match it finds.

cases.name: InvalidEscape
cases.doc: A `\` is followed by something that is not an escape, or ends the pattern.

cases.name: NothingToRepeat
cases.doc: A `*`, `+`, `?` or `{n,m}` has nothing before it to repeat.

cases.name: InvalidRange
cases.doc: A class range ends before it starts, as `z-a` does, or one end of it is a class such as `\d`.

cases.name: InvalidCount
cases.doc: A repetition count is over 1000, or its maximum is below its minimum.

cases.name: UnknownProperty
cases.doc: A `\p{...}` names a property or category this package does not know.

cases.name: UnknownFlag
cases.doc: A `(?...)` holds a flag other than `i`, `m`, `s` and `x`.

cases.name: InvalidGroupName
cases.doc: A group name is empty, or holds something other than letters, digits and `_`, or starts with a digit.

cases.name: DuplicateGroupName
cases.doc: Two groups have the same name.

cases.name: Unsupported
cases.doc: The pattern uses lookaround, a backreference or something else that cannot be matched in linear time.

cases.name: InvalidText
cases.doc: The pattern is not UTF-8 text.

cases.name: TooLarge
cases.doc:
The compiled pattern would be too large, usually from counted repetitions inside each other, or its groups
are nested too deeply.

cases.name: OutOfMemory
cases.doc: The allocator could not supply the storage.

doc.summary: A compiled pattern.
doc.markdown:
A compiled pattern. Not copied.
The syntax is RE2's: literals, `.`, classes such as `[a-z]`, `[^0-9]`, `[[:alpha:]]`, `\d`, `\w` and `\s`,
Unicode general categories and properties such as `\p{L}`, `\p{Lu}` and `\p{White_Space}`, the anchors `^`, `$`,
`\A`, `\z`, `\b` and `\B`, groups `(...)`, `(?:...)` and `(?<name>...)`, alternation `|`, the repetitions `*`,
`+`, `?` and `{n,m}` with a lazy `?` form of each, and the flags `i`, `m`, `s` and `x` as `(?i)` or `(?i:...)`.
Backreferences and lookaround are refused: without them every search takes time linear in the text.
